title: Tokugawa firearms: regulated persistence and changing tasks
summary: Firearms persisted in documented agricultural/hunting and elite niches; regulation and changing social meanings cannot be collapsed into national abandonment.

stages.deployment: Already established technology at the episode’s start; no invention claim.
stages.diffusion: Local ownership registers and qualitative evidence; no national curve.
stages.non-adoption/niche: Continued farming/hunting and elite uses under regulation.
stages.displacement/reversal: Reported shift toward security meanings in the Edo hinterland in the 1840s; does not establish wholesale technological replacement.

counterevidence: No national gun-stock, firing-rate or military-effectiveness series; inherited local records and overlapping scholarly lineage.

episode.technology_configuration: Locally owned matchlock firearms in Tokugawa villages; elite marksmanship considered as a distinct associated task, not the same user population.
episode.task: Protect crops, hunt, display elite martial skill; later reported local-security use.
episode.population: Selected village households and domains represented in historians’ records, especially Shiiba/Matsumoto; Edo-hinterland interpretive subepisode.
episode.interval: 1603–1853; numerical anchors 1745 and 1836, Edo change from 1840s.
contemporary_alternatives: Nonfirearm crop protection/hunting methods: not evaluated in inspected sources
Swords, bows and spears continued in other tasks; not equivalent substitutes for every use
Abstention from firearm possession where permitted or necessary: individual constraints unknown
episode.adoption_measure: 436 recorded firearms/955 Shiiba households in 1745; 586 firearms in 1836 with no same-year household denominator. Qualitative use and licensing evidence elsewhere.
episode.observation_limits: Registers may miss unauthorized guns; stocks do not measure shooters or skill. No representative sample; original records accessed through scholarship.

actors.chooser: Domain and shogunal authorities classify permissible uses; village households seek/hold firearms; elite practitioners choose within status institutions.
actors.payer: Village owners and domain/elite institutions supply resources; prices and fiscal incidence not established.
actors.operator_maintainer: Hunters/cultivators and elite users; gunsmith/repair chain not directly measured.
actors.affected_nonchooser: Other villagers, people subject to armed authority, crops and wildlife; outcomes not systematically counted.
actors.ability_to_refuse: Permission and restrictions vary by class, domain, time and task; legal possession is not proof of free political consent. No individual refusal cohort.

labour.tasks: Hunting/crop protection and elite marksmanship persist; reported later reclassification toward security.
labour.entry_barriers: Permission/status and practical skill; precise cost, training and apprenticeship thresholds unknown.
labour.bargaining_ownership: Household possession and authority over lawful use differ; gains from saved crops and gunsmith income not quantified.
labour.transition: Local stocks separated by decades, not linked individuals; 1840s meaning change known only from Howell abstract.
labour.distribution: Class/domain differences in access documented qualitatively; no wage, household-income or violence-incidence distribution.
labour.evidence_limit: Cannot infer occupational job creation, welfare or modern gun-policy effects from persistence.

title: Yuan paper currency: monetary rules, fiscal pressure and alternatives
summary: Mongol rulers deployed successive paper-currency regimes and administrative supports; long periods of moderate reconstructed inflation coexist with later depreciation, regional diversity and fiscal strain.

stages.invention: Paper currency predates the Yuan; no first-invention claim.
stages.deployment: Silver-backed issues from 1260 and legal-tender/administrative use.
stages.scaling: Expansion across conquered territories, while local alternatives and account units persist.
stages.non-adoption/niche: Regional exceptions, private silver transactions and unequal exchange access.
stages.displacement/reversal: Erosion of convertibility and severe late instability; precise late acceptance rates unavailable.

counterevidence: The inflation series is sparse and reconstructed; no deterministic claim that fiat money or low capacity inevitably doomed the regime.

episode.technology_configuration: State-issued paper notes with changing silver-redemption arrangements; distinguish 1260–76, 1277–1309 and post-1310 regimes.
episode.task: Settle taxes, salaries and commerce; mobilize imperial purchasing power.
episode.population: Imperial note issuers and recorded transactions/prices; Heicheng/Huizhou contracts appear only through Ichimaru abstract.
contemporary_alternatives: Uncoined silver and older metal coins
Regional cowry-shell use in Yunnan reported by scholarship
Barter in later disruption; prevalence unmeasured
Predecessor Song/Jin paper issues, not simultaneous identical configurations
episode.adoption_measure: Legal provisions, recorded taxes/payments, note issuance and sparse price reconstruction; no proportion of transactions conducted in notes.
episode.observation_limits: Money issues are not money stock or acceptance; stock uses assumed attrition. Official exchange rates may differ from market rates; about a dozen commodity observations each underpin interpolated CPI.

actors.chooser: Khan/court and monetary officials choose issues, rules and reserves; merchants and households respond within constraints.
actors.payer: Treasury resources and taxpayers; note holders may bear depreciation, but incidence is unmeasured.
actors.operator_maintainer: Printing/authentication officials, exchange-bureau staff, tax/payroll personnel and merchants.
actors.affected_nonchooser: Salary recipients, creditors/debtors, taxpayers and populations affected by warfare and price changes.
actors.ability_to_refuse: Legal restrictions and Polo’s reported sanctions constrain refusal; continued alternatives show imperfect uniformity. No consent or actual punishment-frequency measure.

labour.tasks: Note authentication, replacement, accounting and exchange administration; Polo describes official work and experts appraising goods.
labour.entry_barriers: Official appointment, knowledge and capital for exchange/commerce; entry conditions and exclusion not quantified.
labour.bargaining_ownership: State controls note rules; merchants/households retain some alternative transactions; distribution of seigniorage and losses unknown.
labour.transition: Regime chronology and annual issues, not worker or household cohorts.
labour.distribution: Regional redemption availability/account units differ; no occupation-specific real-wage or wealth trajectories.
labour.evidence_limit: Neither an index nor tax usability establishes living standards or who gained from monetization.

title: Late-Qing telegraph: strategic networks, contested finance and market effects
summary: A strategically promoted network could remain costly and unreliable for many users while producing detectable price effects through existing traders. Officials and investors had conflicting interests.

stages.deployment: Shanghai–Tianjin line in 1881 and subsequent network additions, within a broader earlier cable history.
stages.diffusion: 64/130 study prefectures connected by 1904; no household adoption curve.
stages.scaling: Growth of offices/routes under state control and merchant operation/finance.
stages.non-adoption/niche: Abstract-level evidence of restricted popular access; continued private messengers/post as alternatives.
stages.displacement/reversal: No claim that letters, couriers or face-to-face trade disappeared.

counterevidence: Timing not randomized; institutional critiques and price studies examine different margins and partly share sources. State choice is not public consent.

episode.technology_configuration: Landline telegraph service with offices, trained operators, coded messages, capital and tariffs; foreign cable connections are background, not identical service.
episode.task: Military/diplomatic coordination and commercial information/order transmission.
episode.population: Official/investor institutions; 130 prefectures reporting high- and medium-grade rice prices in nine provinces; individual customers uncounted.
episode.interval: Institutional episode 1881–1911; before/after economic panel 1870–1904, ending before broader wireless development.
contemporary_alternatives: Official horse-post relay for government messages
Private messengers and letters traveling with waterborne cargo
Continued commercial networks without a local telegraph office
episode.adoption_measure: Binary prefecture office access by year (June assumed in monthly baseline); 64/130 sample prefectures connected by 1904. Price outcomes separate from adoption.
episode.observation_limits: Presence does not imply use, affordability, uptime or message delivery speed. Source has inconsistent 40% prose; explicit counts imply about 49%. Nine-province price panel is not national.

actors.chooser: Qing central/provincial officials and enterprise managers; investors contest terms; traders decide use conditional on service/cost.
actors.payer: State and merchant capital plus tariffs; shareholder returns matter in Yoon’s account; detailed cost allocation not audited.
actors.operator_maintainer: Telegraph operators, coding/decoding staff, line builders and repairers; labor contracts/wages not observed.
actors.affected_nonchooser: Residents along routes and grain buyers/sellers indirectly exposed to price changes; political subjects affected by faster command.
actors.ability_to_refuse: Route policy is not popular choice. Consumers can use slower alternatives if available; price and status restrict access. Evidence concerns investor bargaining, not a general public right of refusal.

labour.tasks: Rapid message handling, coding, maintenance and altered merchant ordering; slower communication continues.
labour.entry_barriers: Equipment/network capital and operator training; literacy/code knowledge relevant but precise recruitment exclusions unknown.
labour.bargaining_ownership: Official control and investor claims conflict; frontline worker bargaining absent from inspected evidence.
labour.transition: Network rollout across decades; no identified displaced courier/operator career panel.
labour.distribution: Different price-volatility effects by prior market risk; no household buyer/seller or occupation-specific welfare measure.
labour.evidence_limit: Cannot turn price effects into net jobs, famine prevention or universal welfare gains.

title: French metrication: standards, mixed measures and legal deadlines
period: 1795–1840 (later coexistence noted only as a coda)
summary: Metric law required material standards and everyday implementation. The 1812 compromise retained metric bases while adapting use; the 1840 deadline did not establish instant complete displacement.

stages.invention: Earlier scientific work and 1799 prototypes are background, not the adoption measure.
stages.deployment: 1795 requirements followed by standard manufacture/distribution and repeated implementation orders.
stages.diffusion: Local archival examples and secondary synthesis; no national use denominator.
stages.non-adoption/niche: Older terms and task measures persist, including alongside official metric practice.
stages.displacement/reversal: 1812 mixed arrangement and its 1837 repeal effective 1840; distinguish legal reversal from actual replacement.

counterevidence: The institutional sources prefer uniform metric standards and sometimes explain resistance by habit; they do not establish all users’ beliefs or the relative weight of alternatives.

episode.technology_configuration: Metric base standards, calibrated weights/measures, conversion tables and inspection; 1812 familiar subdivisions/labels form a distinct mixed retail configuration.
episode.task: Comparable commercial quantities and administrative/legal measurement.
episode.population: Regulated traders/administrators nationally; observed local-practice evidence concentrated in Isère.
episode.interval: 1795–1840; later Isère observations only reject universal completion in 1840.
contemporary_alternatives: Established local weights and task-linked area/capacity measures
episode.adoption_measure: Laws/decrees, reported standards supply, local administrative correspondence and qualitative persistence; no fraction of compliant shops or households.
episode.observation_limits: Legal date, instrument possession, spoken unit and measured quantity are distinct. Surviving correspondence and official reports may privilege problems/enforcement.

actors.chooser: Legislators/executive officials establish rules; scientists/instrument makers define and realize standards; traders/households adapt daily practice.
actors.payer: Public administration and purchasers of instruments; exact division of costs and replacement losses unknown.
actors.operator_maintainer: Instrument makers, inspectors, teachers, shopkeepers, clerks and users performing conversions.
actors.affected_nonchooser: Customers, workers and households transacting under new legal rules; exact groups harmed by rounding or enforcement unmeasured.
actors.ability_to_refuse: Compulsory legal settings restrict lawful refusal; persistence/compromise show implementation negotiation, not a measured majority preference.

labour.tasks: Calibration, instrument production, inspection, teaching and conversion work; replacement of local conventions changes tasks rather than proving job elimination.
labour.entry_barriers: Scientific/instrument expertise and administrative appointment for specialists; learning and replacement costs for users, magnitude unknown.
labour.bargaining_ownership: State determines legal validity; makers/inspectors operationalize it; customer/trader pricing power not measured.
labour.transition: Several decades between mandate and exclusive legal deadline; no worker cohorts or reliable national completion date.
labour.distribution: Urban/rural contrast asserted by local archive synthesis; no income/sex/occupation-specific transition estimates.
labour.evidence_limit: Cannot infer that uniform standards paid for switching costs for every group or that apparent resistance was irrational.
